rounds.text: Laxmi Goldorna House Ltd currently trades at a P/E of 86.4x and a price-to-book ratio of 15.62x, metrics that suggest an extreme valuation relative to the company's underlying assets [E1], [E2]. This pricing is particularly difficult to justify given that compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has plummeted by 57% [E8]. The market's optimism is further challenged by a reverse DCF analysis, which indicates that the current share price requires an unrealistic 29.5% earnings growth rate to be justified, far exceeding the 10.0% base case assumption [E30]. Consequently, a DCF model estimates an intrinsic value of only Rs 50 per share, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -306.4% [E28], [E29]. The stock’s position at only 4% of its 52-week range suggests that market sentiment has already begun to reflect these fundamental pressures [E5]. Conceded: the company maintains an ROCE of 17.0% and an ROE of 19.1% [E6], [E7]. Investors receive no compensation for these risks through dividends, as the yield is 0.00% [E4].

scorecard.note: Computed arithmetically from the citations that survived grounding — no model input.

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 15.62x (price ₹ 203 on a book value of ₹ 13.0).
The stock sits 4% of the way up its 52-week range (195 low to 400 high).
Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is -57%.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 50 per share against a market price of Rs 203.
That leaves a margin of safety of -306.4%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 29.5% earnings growth, against the 10.0% the base case assumes.
